headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0177 — SMTO can't edit this Office file because it contains macros

html:
SMTO-EXE-0177 — SMTO can't edit this Office file because it contains macros

GUID: b3e6d578-24e3-5f51-be61-ef60f0281607
Slug: office-macro-preservation-unsupported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • This Word, Excel or PowerPoint file contains macros (small built-in programs). SMTO can only look at such files, not read their contents in detail or edit them. Your file wasn't changed and its macros weren't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in Word, Excel or PowerPoint and use Save As to save a new copy as a normal Word Document (.docx), Excel Workbook (.xlsx) or PowerPoint Presentation (.pptx). SMTO can only edit or read the details of files without macros, and saving a new copy keeps your original with its macros intact.
  2. In the conversation, ask SMTO to do the same step again, giving it the name and location of the new copy instead of the original. The new copy has no macros, so SMTO can safely open and change it.
  3. If you only need to know what is in the file, such as whether it has macros or how many pages or sheets it has, ask SMTO to inspect the original file instead. Inspecting is the one step SMTO allows on files with macros, because it never runs or changes them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step on the macro-free copy and reports the new file it created.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the file, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove the macros from your only copy of the file; keep the original.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office worker refused a non-inspect operation because the parsed package is macro-enabled (.docm/.xlsm/.pptm suffix, VBA parts, macro-sheet relationships or macro content types).

What this means

  • A parsed package contains macro indicators and the operation goes beyond safe inspect; the worker refuses structural processing that cannot safely preserve those features. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • A parsed package contains macro indicators and the operation goes beyond safe inspect; the worker refuses structural processing that cannot safely preserve those features.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect macro metadata with office.inspect and keep the original intact; macro-enabled extension alone is not the only detection path.

How to fix it

  • Run office.inspect to confirm macro_enabled is true. Have the user save a separate macro-free copy (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx) in a trusted Office application and point the operation at that copy; SMTO never strips, preserves or executes VBA, and only the inspect operation accepts macro-enabled packages.
  • Use office.inspect to inspect macros safely. Create a separate macro-free copy using a trusted application before structural reading or editing; SMTO never strips or executes VBA.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use office.inspect to inspect macros safely. Create a separate macro-free copy using a trusted application before structural reading or editing; SMTO never strips or executes VBA.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately created separate macro-free document is used for supported structural work without executing or silently stripping VBA.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
